facts.text: All runs train GPT-2 small (124M parameters) on 10B tokens of OpenWebText with AdamW and identical hyperparameters.
Stale-update fraction for round-to-nearest BF16 updates: 18.2% at step 1000, 44.7% at step 5000, 61.5% at step 20000; stochastic rounding: 0.0% at every step.

The half-ulp test (update magnitude below half a BF16 ulp of the weight) identifies stale updates with precision 0.98 and recall 0.96; selecting the top 8.7% of gradient norms reaches precision 0.41 and recall 0.37.

Validation loss: stochastic rounding everywhere 3.124; stochastic rounding only on the 8.7% of parameters flagged by the half-ulp test 3.125; the same 8.7% chosen at random 3.171. Random bits drawn relative to rounding everywhere: 0.087.
Validation loss after 10B tokens: FP32 master weights 3.112, BF16 round-to-nearest update 3.205, BF16 stochastic-rounded update 3.124 (perplexity 22.47, 24.66 and 22.74).
Average zero-shot accuracy: FP32 master weights 41.8, BF16 round-to-nearest 39.2, BF16 stochastic-rounded 41.3.
Optimizer state per parameter: 12 bytes with FP32 master weights, 8 bytes with BF16 stochastic-rounded updates.

Synthetic diagnostics report 61.5% stale round-to-nearest updates at step 20000 and half-ulp predictor precision 0.98 and recall 0.96. These descriptive measurements do not establish global training stalling or its cause; a subset of stale updates can coexist with continuing loss improvement.

Synthetic point estimates for stochastic rounding: half-ulp selection of 8.7% of parameters has validation loss 3.125, rounding everywhere 3.124, and random selection of 8.7% of parameters 3.171. Half-ulp selection uses 0.087 of the random bits relative to rounding everywhere. Repeated-run uncertainty and an equivalence margin are unspecified; neither equivalence nor reproducible performance differences are established.

The synthetic full-stochastic-rounding point estimate is validation loss 3.124 versus 3.112 for FP32 master weights, a reported 0.39% gap. This full-SR comparison is distinct from selective SR and does not establish parity; repeated-run uncertainty and an equivalence margin are unspecified.
It recovers 2.1 of the 2.6 accuracy points that round-to-nearest BF16 updates lose.
Removing the FP32 master copy cuts optimizer-state memory from 12 to 8 bytes per parameter, a 33.3% saving.
The half-ulp test keeps its parity with FP32 at 1B parameters and beyond.
